title: Fever in infections and salmonellosis
guide: Day-wise approach: patterns of fever (salmonella step-ladder, malaria chills and rigors with fatigue, leptospirosis/scrub typhus with calf myalgia and conjunctival suffusion in a farmer, dengue with high-grade fever, retro-orbital and occipital pain and vomiting); investigations with CBC, QBC every 12 hours and malaria excluded only after three consecutive negatives; on day 4 start doxycycline 100 mg BD plus co-trimoxazole DS BD for leptospirosis and scrub typhus; salmonellosis week 1 step-ladder fever with relative bradycardia and vague abdominal pain, week 3 ileocaecal hyperplasia with perforation/bleeding and encephalopathy; salient features include the chronic-carrier gallstone complication and a 5-20 day incubation; Widal low positivity in weeks 1-2 and 80-100% by week 3, blood culture 90% positive in week 1, MacConkey agar and Wilson-Blair bismuth sulphite agar with jet-black colonies, rose spots.

title: Typhoid treatment and dengue
guide: Typhoid pathogenesis: bloodstream to liver, spleen and bone marrow, seeding of gallbladder, biliary system and bowel lymphatics, re-entry causing ileocaecal hyperplasia; uncomplicated therapy co-trimoxazole DS BD 14 days or azithromycin 1 g OD 7 days, complicated therapy ceftriaxone 2 g IV 14 days; dengue incubation 7-10 days, NS1 positive days 1-3 and negative from day 4 when fever subsides and rash appears, falling platelets (not below 50,000) and leucopenia in dengue without warning signs; days 4-7 are the most crucial with bleeding and capillary leak (pleural/pericardial effusion, ascites), monitored by blood pressure with IV fluids, IVC diameter and haematocrit, transfusing platelets below 10,000 or below 20,000 with bleeding, no steroids; febrile, critical and recovery phases with IgM positive from day 5.

title: Leptospirosis, scrub typhus and the malaria life cycle
guide: Leptospirosis: abrupt low-to-intermediate fever, calf muscle tenderness, conjunctival congestion and suffusion, 4-7 days as the vital period, hepatorenal syndrome (hepatitis with jaundice plus ATN), non-oliguric AKI with hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia, thrombocytopenia, myocarditis with secondary MR/AR, aseptic meningitis, ARDS and rhabdomyolysis; modified Faine's criteria with MAT as gold standard; doxycycline plus ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD. Scrub typhus: Orientia tsutsugamushi, micro-infarcts in kidney with a thrombotic microangiopathic pattern, no immunological phase, eschar, lymphadenopathy at the end of one week, untreated CNS involvement within one week with reversible sensorineural deafness, opsoclonus and myoclonus, treated with doxycycline 100 mg BD 7 days or azithromycin 500 mg OD 5 days. Malaria cycle: sporozoites via blood to liver, pre-erythrocytic schizogony, merozoite release, erythrocytic schizogony and fever.

title: Malaria: features, species and treatment
guide: Extreme fatigue, tachypnoea/tachycardia/splenomegaly and mild myalgia in uncomplicated disease; complications from cyto-adherence, rosetting and agglutination of RBCs with organ ischaemia and the spleen as the major trapping organ; species table — falciparum (younger cells, 48 h, black pigment, no relapses), vivax (reticulocytes and cells up to 2 weeks old, 48 h, yellow-brown, relapses), ovale (reticulocytes, 48 h, dark-brown, relapses), malariae (older cells, 72 h, brown-black, no relapses); complicated falciparum disease with anaemia, cerebral malaria, hypoglycaemia, shock, black water fever and jaundice; diagnosis by thick smear with Giemsa and light microscopy as gold standard, thin smear not sensitive, QBC with acridine orange and three tests 12 hours apart to exclude malaria, HRP2 rapid test not validated; oral artemether 80 mg plus lumefantrine 480 mg four tablets BD for 3 days first line with atovaquone-proguanil, clindamycin-mefloquine, doxycycline-quinine, artesunate-amodiaquine and artesunate-mefloquine as alternatives; complicated disease IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12 and 24 hours then daily on days 2 and 3.
